<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Deum magnum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> God is the great Lord * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.

b.25accb639b:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>U</c>ndécimo Kaléndas Augústi Luna duodevicésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>pud Massíliam, in Gállia, natális sanctæ Maríæ Magdalénæ, de qua Dóminus eiécit septem dæmónia, et quæ ipsum Salvatórem a mórtuis resurgéntem prima vidére méruit.
<h>P</h>hilíppis, in Macedónia, sanctæ Synthýches, cuius méminit beátus Paulus Apóstolus.
<h>A</h>ncýræ, in Galátia, natális sancti Platónis Mártyris, qui, sub Agrippíno Vicário, verbéribus cæsus, uncis laniátus férreis, aliísque immaníssimis tormentórum genéribus cruciátus, demum, abscísso cápite, invíctam ánimam Deo réddidit. Ipsíus vero mirácula in subveniéndis captívis, Acta secúndæ Sýnodi Nicǽnæ testántur.
<h>I</h>n Cypro sancti Theóphili Prætóris, qui ab Arábibus tentus, et, cum nec donis nec minis flecti posset ut Christum negáret, gládio cæsus est.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Cyrílli Epíscopi, doctrína et sanctitáte conspícui.
<h>M</h>enáti, in território Arvernénsi, sancti Meneléi Abbátis.
<h>I</h>n monastério Fontanéllæ, in Gállia, sancti Wandregísili Abbátis, miráculis clari; cuius corpus ad Blandínum monastérium, in Flándria, póstea delátum fuit.
<h>U</h>lyssipóne, in Lusitánia, sancti Lauréntii a Brundúsio, Sacerdótes et Confessóris; qui Ordinis Minórum sancti Francísci Capuccinórum Miníster éxstitit Generális, atque, divíni verbi prædicatióne et árduis pro Dei glória gestis præclárus, Leóne Décimo tértio, Summo Pontífice, Sanctórum fastis adscríptus est.
<h>S</h>cythópoli, in Palæstína, sancti Ioséphi Cómitis.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.2ecc0f4cd1:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>uly 22nd 2027, the 18th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Marseilles, holy Mary Magdalen, out of whom the Lord cast seven devils, and who was made worthy to be the first to see this same Saviour after that He was risen from the dead.
<h>A</h>t Philippi, holy Syntyche, of whom mention is made by the blessed Apostle Paul.
<h>A</h>t Ancyra, in Galatia, the holy martyr Plato, [in the year 304.]
<h>U</h>nder the Vicar Agrippinus he was cut with stripes, pronged with iron nails, and tormented with other dire sorts of torments, then at last beheaded, and so gave up his soul unconquered to God. The miracles wrought by him in the succouring of prisoners are attested by the acts of the Second Council of Nicea.
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, the holy Praetor Theophilus. The Arabs strove to make him deny Christ, but as neither bribery nor threats could bend him, they slew him with the sword, [in the year 790.]
<h>A</h>t Antioch, holy Cyril, Bishop [of that see,] famous for his teaching and holiness, [in the year 300.]
<h>I</h>n Auvergne, the holy Abbot Menelaus, [about the year 700, Restorer of the Abbey of Menat, in the Diocese of Clermont.]
<h>I</h>n the Monastery of the Blandijnberg, in Gent in Flanders, holy Wandregisilus [St. Wandrille], Abbot of Fontenelle, [in the year 667, the founder of several monasteries.]
<h>A</h>t Lisbon, the holy Confessor Laurence of Brindisi, Minister-General of the Order of Capuchin Friars Minors of St. Francis. He was famous for his preaching of the word of God, and for his hard work for God's glory, and the Supreme Pontiff Leo XIII enrolled his name among those of the saints.
<h>A</h>t Bethshan, in Palestine, the holy Earl Joseph, [about the year 366.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>áteant aures misericórdiæ tuæ, Dómine, précibus supplicántium: et, ut peténtibus desideráta concédas; fac eos, quæ tibi sunt plácita, postuláre.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.3184ae7c86:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>L</c>et thy merciful ears, O Lord, be open to the prayers of thy humble servants; and, that they may obtain their petitions, make them to ask such things as shall please thee.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio S. Praxedis Virginis</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Veni, elécta mea, et ponam in te thronum meum; quia concupívit Rex spéciem tuam.

<r>℣.</r> Adducéntur Regi Vírgines post eam.
<r>℟.</r> Próximæ eius afferéntur tibi.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>xáudi nos, Deus, salutáris noster: ut sicut de beátæ Praxédis festivitáte gaudémus; ita piæ devotiónis erudiámur afféctu.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

<r>Commemoration of St. Praxedes, Virgin</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Come, O My chosen one, and I will establish My throne in thee, for the King hath greatly desired thy beauty.

<r>℣.</r> After her shall virgins be brought unto the King.
<r>℟.</r> Her fellows shall be brought unto thee.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>raciously hear us, O God of our salvation; that as we rejoice in the festivity of blessed Praxedes, we may be instructed in the affections of a loving devotion.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
